objectives: Hear /d/ followed immediately by /r/ at the beginning of a taught word.
Blend /d/ and /r/ smoothly without adding a vowel between them.
Distinguish the initial dr blend from /d/ alone and other taught blends.
Say the complete word after blending the onset with the remaining sounds.
concepts: The initial dr blend contains /d/ followed by /r/.
Both consonant sounds remain audible in the blend.
No extra vowel belongs between /d/ and /r/.
Listening for the whole word confirms accurate blending.

definitions.definition: Two consonant sounds heard together at the beginning of a word.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.
Joining speech sounds in order to say a word.

workedExamples.solution: Drum starts with /d/ followed by /r/; duck starts with /d/ alone.
Keep /d/ and /r/ together, then blend /ɪ/ and /p/.

commonMistakes: Adding a vowel and saying duh-rum instead of blending smoothly.
Leaving out /r/ and saying dum for drum.
Guessing before hearing the whole word.
keyTakeaways: Do not insert a vowel between the consonants.
Blend the onset with the rest of the word.
Check the complete word against the sounds.
revisionPoints: Drum and drip both begin with dr.
